items.title: @rohanpaul_ai：New Amazon paper shows that an LLM can act as a research world model, predicting whether a training change will help bef
items.abstract_or_text: New Amazon paper shows that an LLM can act as a research world model, predicting whether a training change will help before anyone spends GPU time on it. AI research agents can propose experiments far faster than teams can afford to run them. Choosing what gets GPU time means guessing outcomes in advance. They used an LLM as a research world model that predicts an experiment's gain before it runs. They tested it on 2,653 real experiment records from 9 setups, from pretraining to inference. Past records from the same setup raised average ranking correlation with actual results from 0.506 to 0.774 across 5 setups. On the OLMo3-100M setup, adding records at low reasoning effort scored 0.892, while max effort without records reached 0.648. If you run research agents, log every experiment, including failures, and feed those records to whatever model picks the next run.

items.title: @zwljohnny：ReplaySSM now runs in production in GLM-5.3-Flash and Kimi-K3, and ships in TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, FlashInfer, and SGLang!
items.abstract_or_text: ReplaySSM now runs in production in GLM-5.3-Flash and Kimi-K3, and ships in TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, FlashInfer, and SGLang! It speeds up standard decoding (up to 1.47x) and speculative decoding (up to 2.1x), and now also enables a low-precision SSM state whose rounding error never propagates through the recurrence. Building on our earlier ReplaySSM work, we collaborated with @NVIDIA to pin down what the method really unlocks. Caching SSM inputs instead of the state is what ReplaySSM does. What it changes is that computing the output and updating the state can be separated during decoding. All three gains follow from that separation. Joint blog post, paper, and code with @NVIDIA and @tri_dao 👇

items.title: @IamKyros69：Terence Tao just published a 27 slide deck saying the AI math hype only shows you the wins.. every week you see a new po
items.abstract_or_text: Terence Tao just published a 27 slide deck saying the AI math hype only shows you the wins.. every week you see a new post.. AI solved an open math problem.. Tao says that feed hides most of the story.. the failed attempts never get posted.. the compute bill never gets posted.. and most frontier problems are STILL unsolved.. then he went further.. blindly chasing more solved problems is now hurting math.. open problems were never the goal.. they were lighthouses.. the real value was everything mathematicians learned on the way there.. let AI jump straight to the answer and the whole journey disappears.. in 1976 Appel and Haken proved the four color theorem using a computer.. and many mathematicians refused to accept it because no human could check it by hand.. 50 years later the fear has flipped.. the computer is right.. but nobody understands WHY.. so Tao asks you one question.. if an AI cured cancer and passed every trial.. would you inject it before a single human understood how it works.. you spent centuries thinking math was about answers.. answers are now cheap.. understanding is the new scarce thing

items.abstract_or_text: Teams are already generating Lean proofs, so why can't we generate human proofs with diagrams and deeper explanations? Terence Tao recently criticized auto-research for leaving behind mathematicians and losing understanding, but this is also a problem agents can solve now. I'm not suggesting researchers should understand the massive Lean proofs, but rather get agents to generate abstractions to understand it enough to guide the next steps. It might take longer, but certainly not longer than humans deriving the proofs from scratch. The results are remarkable: 🔹 9 of 353 open Erdős problems solved 🔹 44 of 492 open OEIS conjectures proved 🔹 Two problems resolved after 56 years 🔹 New results in optimization, algebraic geometry, graph theory and quantum optics. 📄 Tsoukalas G, Kovsharov A, Shirobokov S, et al.
